audit_scope.description: This batch predominantly covers Execution Layer logic: EVM opcode execution (bitwise, stack operations), state transitions (fork activations for Tangerine Whistle, Spurious Dragon, Byzantium), gas economics, P2P networking (eth/69→eth/70), and provider APIs. CL is only tangentially referenced in EIP-7568 (Shapella coordination) but not materially in scope for this batch.

in_scope: EVM Opcode Execution (bitwise, stack, shift operations)
State Transition (fork activations: Tangerine Whistle, Spurious Dragon, Byzantium)

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion attacks, replay attacks across chains
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks/transactions, request pre-PoS data to waste resources
Deploy contracts exploiting underpriced opcodes for DoS, oversized contract code, stack manipulation attacks
Intercept or modify provider requests, phishing via fake provider injection

cl_vectors.threat: Propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations (slashing condition), censorship

cl_vectors.entry_point: External APIs (e.g., MEV-Boost relay, checkpoint sync endpoint)
cl_vectors.threat: Provide incorrect data, censorship, denial of service

misclassified_entities.reason: Parent block is internal blockchain state data, not an external entity. It is the previously validated block stored in the local chain.
Transaction execution is an internal process within the EVM, not an external entity. The external entity is the transaction sender/submitter.
The node operator is the local administrator of the system under audit, not an external entity sending data into it. They configure the node but do not interact via a network boundary.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P (devp2p eth/69-70)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network (devp2p): GetBlockBodies (0x05), BlockBodies (0x06), GetReceipts (0x0f), Receipts (0x10)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Any node can connect and send arbitrary protocol messages including requests for pre-PoS data, invalid blocks, or malformed messages. Covers EXT-PEER-NODES, EXT-REQUESTING-PEER, EXT-NETWORK-PEER, EXT-PEER from source files.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner) via P2P
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network: Block propagation (NewBlock, NewBlockHashes messages)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miners are unauthenticated P2P participants. Blocks they produce must be fully validated (PoW, difficulty, state roots, transaction validity). Covers EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER, EXT-MINER from source files.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. All transaction fields (nonce, gas, value, data, signature, chain ID) must be validated. Covers EXT-TX-SENDER, EXT-USER (EIP-607), EXT-DEVELOPER (EIP-2657).

trusted_external_entities.name: Replay Attacker via P2P/RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network and JSON-RPC: submitting transactions signed for other chains
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker attempts to replay transactions from other chains (e.g., ETC). Chain ID validation (EIP-155) is the defense. Covers EXT-ATTACKER from EIP-607 and EIP-608.

trusted_external_entities.name: DoS Attacker via Transaction Submission
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC / P2P: crafted transactions with underpriced IO operations
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker crafts transactions exploiting underpriced opcodes to cause resource exhaustion. Gas repricing (EIP-150/608) is the defense. Covers EXT-ATTACKER from EIP-608.

trusted_external_entities.name: Genesis Configuration Server (yolonet.xyz)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External web server providing genesis configuration. No authentication mechanism specified. Compromised server could provide malicious genesis config leading to joining a fake network. Covers EXT-GENESIS-SERVER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum Foundation Bootnode via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Bootnode is an unauthenticated P2P endpoint. While operated by EF, the enode address could be spoofed or the bootnode compromised. Peer lists returned must not be blindly trusted. Covers EXT-EF-BOOTNODE.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethstats Monitoring Server
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External monitoring service. Data flows outbound (node → server), but a compromised stats server could potentially influence node behavior through response data. Covers EXT-ETHSTATS-SERVER.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Injected EthereumProvider
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps interact via the injected provider interface. Any web page can attempt to call provider methods. Authorization checks (error 4001, 4100) are required for sensitive operations. Covers EXT-DAPP.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Browser Extension
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Browser extension injection: window.ethereum / EthereumProvider object
trusted_external_entities.rationale: While the wallet is installed by the user, a malicious extension could inject a fake provider. The DApp has no way to authenticate the provider's origin. Covers EXT-WALLET-EXTENSION, EXT-MALICIOUS-SCRIPT.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Ethereum Node via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC over HTTP/WebSocket: provider forwards requests to remote node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The remote node processing requests from the provider is not authenticated from the DApp's perspective. Responses could be manipulated by a MITM or malicious RPC endpoint. Covers EXT-ETHEREUM-NODE.

trusted_external_entities.name: End User via Wallet UI
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Wallet UI: user approval/rejection of transaction requests
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users can reject requests (error 4001) but may also be social-engineered into approving malicious transactions. The system cannot trust user decisions are informed. Covers EXT-USER from EIP-2696.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: All incoming P2P requests must be validated for scope (post-PoS blocks only in eth/70), message format, and rate-limited to prevent resource exhaustion. Pre-PoS data requests must be rejected.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P Block Processing: NewBlock, BlockBodies messages
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block validation required: PoW verification, difficulty check (with bomb delay), header field validation (sequential numbering, timestamp, gas limit), state/receipt/transaction root verification, ommer validation.

Full transaction validation required: intrinsic gas check, ECDSA signature recovery, nonce match, balance sufficiency (gas*price + value), sender must be EOA, chain ID verification (EIP-155), contract code size limit (EIP-170).

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction Validation: Chain ID extraction from v value
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Chain ID must be extracted from signature v value (chainId = (v-35)/2) and verified against current network chain ID. Transactions with mismatched chain IDs must be rejected (EIP-155).

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM Gas Metering: IO opcode gas schedule
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Gas costs for IO-heavy opcodes (SLOAD, BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, CALL, etc.) must accurately reflect resource consumption. EIP-150 repricing must be active post-block 2,463,000. Insufficient gas must halt execution.

Genesis configuration integrity should be verified (hash check or signature). Without verification, a compromised server could supply a malicious genesis that forks the node onto an attacker-controlled chain.
Peer lists from bootnode must not be blindly trusted. Node should verify peers through additional discovery mechanisms and not rely on single bootnode. Eclipse attack prevention required.

Stats reporting should be one-directional (outbound only). Node must not accept commands or configuration changes from the stats server. Sensitive data (private keys, internal state) must not be leaked.

Provider must enforce authorization for sensitive methods (account access, signing). Must return proper error codes (4001 user rejected, 4100 unauthorized, 4200 unsupported). Must not expose private keys or internal wallet state.
DApps should verify provider authenticity where possible. Multiple injected providers must be handled safely. Malicious extensions could inject fake providers to intercept transactions.

Responses from remote nodes must be validated. A malicious or compromised RPC endpoint could return incorrect block data, fake transaction receipts, or manipulated state. TLS should be used for transport security.

User approval does not validate transaction correctness. Wallet must clearly display transaction details (recipient, value, data) to enable informed consent. Social engineering attacks remain possible.
